analysis.title: GS Basics: Sentiment Reset. Energy Headwinds. Positioning Color
key_insights: Overnight reversal: KOSPI down about 3.5%, China near a bear market, broad weakness across semiconductors, following a rally on SpaceX and Supermicro the day before.
LRCX reported strong numbers but struggled to clear elevated whisper expectations, and guidance offered limited upside. Semi capex is under pressure, with Tokyo Electron down 6.99%.
Tesla cut FY capex guidance from more than $25bn to about $20bn, out of sync with SpaceX's message earlier in the week. The market does not like capex going backwards.
Meta lifted the bottom end of its FY capex guidance to $135bn, which implies about $49-59bn of spending in Q4. That is an ambitious ramp.
TI reported broad-based analog recovery and robust data center demand, but the stock did not move much.

DeepSeek's open source DeepInfer promises materially better inference efficiency on existing infrastructure, raising questions about how much incremental compute is needed. Privorotsky says none of this is thesis breaking but it is enough to unsettle a fragile tape.
Two critical PHP vulnerabilities, each scored 9.2/10 with remote code execution possible, have emergency patches released. Privorotsky wonders whether cybersecurity finally catches a bid.
Bonds are firmly bid as AI sells off. AI weakness reprices the capex cycle, eases prospective issuance pressure and becomes a growth shock, so the equity problem helps with the rates problem.
Institutional accounts in New York describe fatigue and caution on tech. Prime flow data showed one of the most pronounced net tech reductions in recent memory.

Managers appear to have cut net exposure while keeping gross intact. They are far less allocated to AI names than earlier this year, but none Privorotsky met are outright short. Year-end focus is capital preservation.
Most accounts still believe AI demand is robust, but questions have entered on capital availability, the ability to energize capacity and the sustainability of spending.

Energy: hopes of de-escalation are fading, diplomatic pathways are narrowing, and press reports suggest renewed escalation could follow the midterms. This complicates the usual post-midterm positive equity pattern.
Punitive energy prices remain a significant headwind for equities and a reason to stay cautious.
AI demand indicators remain strong: token consumption keeps growing, B200 compute spot pricing is breaking out, and SpaceX cites sub one year paybacks on new compute deployments.

Two opposing concerns coexist: that the industry cannot deliver projected gigawatts (high 40s estimated for 2027 versus possible delivery in the low 20s), and that too much capacity gets delivered for inference demand to absorb.
Other worries include midterm and energy risk, rates, credit stress and French sovereign spreads. Credit is increasingly setting the tone.

Privorotsky argues the economy has moved from a savings glut to a spending glut, which probably demands lower multiples and greater certainty on future cash flows, and neither helps equities in the short term.
Credit spreads and availability of financing are becoming increasingly important signals to watch.

sector_views.rationale: Institutions are de-risking net tech exposure and the tape is fragile, while the AI demand side still looks robust.
High energy prices and escalation risk after the midterms are a headwind for equities.

risk_factors: Fading de-escalation hopes and possible renewed escalation after the midterms, including retaliation against energy infrastructure.
High energy prices as a headwind for equities.
Credit stress and tightening financing availability.
Capex guidance volatility (Tesla cut, Meta ramp) and DeepSeek inference efficiency questioning compute needs.
Power and gigawatt delivery shortfalls versus overbuild concerns.
PHP vulnerabilities as a cybersecurity complication for risk sentiment.
Year-end capital preservation and performance lock-in by managers.
vol_and_positioning: Aggregated prime flow data showed one of the most pronounced net tech reductions in recent memory.
Managers appear to have cut net exposure while keeping gross intact.
Participants are far less allocated to AI names than earlier this year, and none met are outright short.
A side note says AI exposure is very low on a 1-year lookback but still above the historical baseline.
geopolitical: Hopes of de-escalation are fading and diplomatic pathways are narrowing, with press reports that renewed escalation could follow the midterms.
Retaliation against energy infrastructure remains a real possibility.

tension_points.bull_case: Token consumption continues to grow, B200 compute spot pricing is breaking out, SpaceX cites sub one year paybacks, and hyperscalers say demand and monetization are accelerating.
tension_points.bear_case: Concerns over power delivery, overbuilt capacity, capex going backwards, DeepSeek inference efficiency, and credit availability for funding spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit spreads widening and financing availability tightening.

theme_stances.key_argument: Capex guidance swings, DeepSeek efficiency and institutional de-risking have unsettled a fragile tape, though AI demand remains robust.
theme_stances.evidence: None of this feels thesis breaking, but it is enough to unsettle a fragile tape.
